elements.element: Vendor has an express duty to defend Customer and its affiliates.
elements.evidence: Section 16.2 chapeau now reads "Array shall defend, indemnify and hold harmless each of Ono, its Affiliates and Sublicensees...", and the inserted sentence repeats "Array shall further defend and indemnify the Ono Indemnitees"; the Ono Indemnitees definition expressly includes Affiliates.

elements.element: Vendor indemnifies Customer and its affiliates against third-party claims.
elements.evidence: Retained 16.2: "from and against any and all Liabilities from any Third Party Claims incurred by any Ono Indemnitee", with Ono Indemnitees defined to include Ono, its Affiliates and Sublicensees.

elements.element: Vendor indemnity covers claims that Services or Deliverables infringe intellectual property rights.
elements.evidence: Inserted sentence: "against any Third Party Claim alleging that the Array Patents, Array Know-How or Products supplied by Array infringe any intellectual property right" \u2014 the licence/supply analogue of services and deliverables, and the "notwithstanding Section 11.4" carve-out stops the retained own-expense defence rule from cancelling it.

elements.element: Vendor indemnity covers Vendor's breach of applicable law.
elements.evidence: Inserted sentence: "or arising from Array's breach of Law". Note the new 16.1 head uses "applicable Law" while 16.2 uses "Law"; if the Agreement defines only "Applicable Law"/"Laws", conform the capitalisation to the defined term.

elements.element: Vendor indemnity covers a data breach caused by Vendor.
elements.evidence: Inserted sentence: "any unauthorized access to or disclosure of Ono Confidential Information caused by Array" \u2014 the Customer Data analogue in this licence agreement.

elements.element: Vendor indemnity covers Vendor's gross negligence and wilful misconduct.
elements.evidence: Inserted sentence ends "or Array's gross negligence or willful misconduct"; the retained Ono-side gross-negligence carve-out in the (b)-(d) list applies to Ono Indemnitee misconduct only and does not contradict this head.

elements.element: The indemnification procedure requires notice of a claim.
elements.evidence: Section 16.3 (untouched): Indemnitee "shall promptly notify the other Party (the \"Indemnitor\") in writing of any Third Party Claim"; 16.3 applies to "indemnification under this Article 16", so it reaches the new heads in 16.2.

elements.element: The indemnification procedure allocates control of the defence.
elements.evidence: Section 16.3: "the Indemnitor shall have sole control of the defense and/or settlement thereof", with information and settlement-consent mechanics retained.

elements.element: The indemnification procedure requires reasonable cooperation.
elements.evidence: Section 16.3: "The Indemnitee ... shall cooperate fully with the Indemnitor and its legal representatives in the investigation of any action with respect to a Third Party Claim covered by this indemnification."

elements.element: Customer indemnity is limited to Customer-provided content and Customer's breach of law.
elements.evidence: Section 16.1 heads are now only "(a) any materials, data or other content provided by Ono to Array; and (b) any breach of applicable Law by Ono", with the favourable Array-misconduct carve-out retained; the former commercialisation, Clinical Study and Article 15 heads are removed.

elements.element: Vendor indemnifies Customer against third-party intellectual-property claims.
elements.evidence: Inserted 16.2 sentence covers Third Party Claims alleging that Array Patents, Array Know-How or Array-supplied Products infringe any intellectual property right.

elements.element: The IP indemnity may exclude infringement caused by Customer modifications.
elements.evidence: Permissive element: no modification exclusion is imposed, which is permitted (and more favourable to us); condition does not apply.

elements.element: The IP indemnity may exclude infringement caused by Customer combinations.
elements.evidence: Permissive element: no combination exclusion appears; its absence does not defeat the element.

elements.element: The IP indemnity may exclude infringement caused by Customer specifications.
elements.evidence: Permissive element: no specification exclusion appears; its absence does not defeat the element.

elements.element: Vendor must procure continued use, modify, or replace the infringing item.
elements.evidence: No procure/modify/replace remedy ladder appears anywhere in the rendered 16.1-16.3 or in Section 11.4.

elements.element: Vendor must refund applicable fees if procure, modify, or replace remedies are unavailable.
elements.evidence: No refund-of-fees backstop is drafted; the operative language contains no payment-return mechanic tied to unavailable remedies.

elements.element: Vendor's indemnity is subject to a super-cap of three times annual fees.
elements.evidence: No 3x annual fees super-cap (or any indemnity cap) is inserted in Article 16.

reasons: Preferred level is complete on the operative text: "defend" added to the 16.2 chapeau, a single inserted sentence adding the four missing heads (IP infringement, breach of Law, Array-caused disclosure of Ono Confidential Information, gross negligence/willful misconduct), Section 16.3's notice/control/cooperation mechanics left intact, and 16.1 narrowed to Ono-supplied content and Ono's breach of Law.
Fallback is incomplete (no procure/modify/replace ladder, no refund backstop, no 3x annual fees super-cap), but that is immaterial because the position is complete at the preferred level.

Minimality holds: the edits are confined to the checklist items, favourable retained language (the Array-misconduct carve-out in 16.1, the Ono-misconduct carve-out in 16.2, all of 16.3) survives, and no survival tail, expense language or extra damages categories were bolted on. The "notwithstanding Section 11.4" phrase is narrow and necessary \u2014 without it the retained rule that the Subject Party defends Infringement Actions "in its sole discretion and at its own expense" would contradict the new defend-and-indemnify obligation \u2014 so it is not a broad override.

Intent is preserved: Section 11.4's control mechanics, the settlement-consent and notice-prejudice provisions, and the Ono-Indemnitee misconduct exception all continue to operate without contradiction; the narrowing of 16.1 is required by the tenth preferred element rather than an unrelated reallocation.

Drafting point to tidy before sending (not a level failure): align the capitalisation of "Law" in the new 16.2 sentence with the Agreement's defined term as used in the new 16.1(b) ("applicable Law"), so the new heads do not rest on an inconsistently rendered term.

Commercial heads-up for the negotiation, not a checklist defect: removing Ono's product-liability and Clinical Study indemnity heads from 16.1 is a material shift in a licence where Ono commercialises in its own territory; expect Array to push back and be ready to trade that narrowing against the new IP head.
